gaps.sentence: You ___ to apply for a visa before you travel; the airline will check it.
gaps.explanation: 'Need to' expresses necessity and, unlike 'must', takes 'to': need to apply.

gaps.sentence: I ___ help thinking he is hiding something.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't help' plus -ing means being unable to stop a feeling: can't help thinking.

gaps.sentence: Students ___ to hand in essays by Friday at the latest.
gaps.hint: ought to takes the full infinitive
gaps.explanation: 'Ought to' takes the full infinitive, so only 'ought' fits before 'to': ought.

gaps.sentence: I do not know whose coat this is — it ___ belong to one of the guests.
gaps.explanation: 'Might' hedges a guess when the speaker is not sure: might belong.

gaps.sentence: Students ___ to buy the textbook; copies are available in the library.
gaps.explanation: 'Don't have to' plus the infinitive expresses absence of obligation: don't have to buy.

gaps.sentence: You really ___ to apologise before this gets worse.
gaps.explanation: 'Ought to' expresses advice similar to 'should': ought to apologise.

gaps.sentence: It is the only blue house on the street, so you ___ miss it.
gaps.explanation: 'You can't miss it' is an idiom meaning it is impossible not to find: can't.

gaps.sentence: The theatre was completely empty, so the performance ___ have been very popular.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have' draws a negative conclusion from evidence: can't have been.
